claim_being_audited: Whether the current release can be certified under the model-card disclosure policy despite a newly observed small-business onboarding regression, based on aggregate readiness evidence, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, prior approval context, and informal post-launch monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use `suspicious` when some admissible evidence supports the actor's direction but a required policy predicate or support link is missing.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness but do not, by themselves, satisfy the disclosure-policy requirement.
The governing policy text requires current-release documentation of material weaknesses or approved mitigation; the available evidence shows neither.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring can provide context only and cannot substitute for current evidence or reviewed risk acceptance.
evidence_requests: Current-release model-card or launch documentation showing explicit disclosure of the small-business onboarding limitation for the named launch use case.
Approved mitigation or risk-acceptance record tied to this release, with reviewer/owner sign-off and date.
Current evaluation artifact showing the subgroup regression has been resolved or no longer meets the policy's materiality threshold.
Any formal disclosure language or customer/internal release note referenced by the actor but not included in the admissible evidence.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence shows a current material segment weakness: the small-business onboarding slice is 1.3 percentage points below the warning threshold.
The policy requires material segment weaknesses in the current release to be disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation before certification.
The record contains only an informal monitoring comment and explicitly lacks reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language.
Prior approval predates the current retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release support requirement.
The actor's packet acknowledges the key gap, which means the central policy predicate for certification remains unresolved.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the present record without attached current-release disclosure or approved mitigation for the subgroup regression.
That prior approval of the same model family provides more than contextual support for the current certification decision.
That public AI-risk and model-card guidance, by themselves, establish compliance with the stated internal release policy.
